Subject: Lumina Dedicated: capacity pacing, spot-bursting & preemption SLA

Hi team —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, I'm starting a short thread to align on how we'll size your Dedicated GPU pool and the burst/autoscale policy during Q4 peaks. Attached is the forecast spreadsheet we discussed — can you confirm the MAU and peak concurrent inference rows (sheet: "ops_forecast") so we can map to GPU capacity?

Key asks from our side:
- Finalized expected peak concurrent requests per minute for Nov/Dec (hourly percentiles if available)
- Tolerance for preemption: are you comfortable with preemptible/spot-backed burst capacity for up to 10% of peak?
- Any strict SLA windows where preemption is unacceptable (e.g., billing close, demos, investor events)

I've attached a short draft playbook that outlines how Redwood configures ephemeral spot bursts and crediting during incidents. This is an initial proposal — Karthik and Ben will add the headroom matrix once we get your numbers.

Attachments: lumina_mau_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_lumina_capacity_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor

Subject: Re: Lumina Dedicated: capacity pacing, spot-bursting & preemption SLA

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the note. We've populated the forecast file (see attached) with conservative and aggressive scenarios — the aggressive column reflects the expected marketing-driven spike in mid-Nov. A couple of questions for clarity:

1) What eviction rate should we budget for when using spot-backed burst capacity? We saw a vendor estimate of 4-6% but want Redwood's operational expectation.
2) For our monthly SLA reporting, we need clarity on how burst hours are attributed and how burst credits would be applied when preemption occurs.
3) Do you support a short warm pool (5–10 min) to avoid cold-start penalties when bursting?

We'd like to keep the core Dedicated pool non-preemptible for baseline traffic and allow up to 15% spike capacity on preemptible instances if the economics are favorable.

Attached: lumina_mau_forecast_Q3-Q4_completed.xlsx

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Lumina Dedicated: capacity pacing, spot-bursting & preemption SLA

Team —

I've reviewed Lumina's forecast. High-level proposal for our sizing/behavior:

- Baseline pool: size to cover P95 of predictable traffic (non-preemptible) — reduces SLA risk and covers steady traffic.
- Shoulder/warm pool: a small set of pre-warmed instances (approx 5–10% of baseline) kept ready to accept traffic with warm caches; uses reserved-but-idle pricing slab.
- Spot/ephemeral burst: allow up to 15% additional capacity on preemptible instances during spikes; assume a 5% eviction rate as operational baseline (we can tune upward once we see Lumina's historical spot stability in the region).
- Autoscale triggers: scale-up when 5-min queue depth > X or avg token-latency exceeds 80th pct target; scale-down with conservative cooldown (10–15m) to avoid oscillation.
- Credit/attribution model: when preemption causes request retries/falls back to baseline, we offer proportional burst credits tied to affected request count (proposal to be drafted by Marissa).

Open items: exact numeric headroom matrix (Ben), pricing impact & credit model (Marissa), warm-pool sizing tied to cache-warming latency (Grace + Lumina SRE).

I'll draft a quick-runbook snippet for the ops team once we lock the headroom numbers.

- Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Lumina Dedicated: capacity pacing, spot-bursting & preemption SLA

Adding the headroom/runbook detail:

- Headroom matrix (baseline to burst):
  * Baseline = P95 traffic -> N baseline GPUs
  * Warm pool = max(ceil(0.08 * N), 2) GPUs (keeps KV caches hot for top 20 prompts)
  * Spot burst cap = ceil(0.15 * N) GPUs (preemptible)

- Eviction planning: assume 5% evictions per 24h for spot due to AZ maintenance and preemption events; we'll schedule staggered replenishment and soft-fallback to baseline without dropping requests (graceful traffic shedding to lower-cost model if pressure > 110% of burst capacity).

- Runbook sketches:
  1) Detection: autoscaler observes sustained 3-min CPU/GPU queue > threshold -> increase by 1 GPU bundle (fast path)
  2) Warm-pool activation: if predicted spike detected from traffic hook, promote warm pool to active and spin spot instances in parallel
  3) Eviction event: if spot loss > 2 instances in < 5m window, trigger immediate throttling policy and notify Lumina SRE; begin proportional credit tagging

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF_shared_playbooks (internal runbook folder)

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Dedicated Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Lumina Dedicated: capacity pacing, spot-bursting & preemption SLA

Thanks — pricing & credits notes from my side:

- We model preemptible burst at ~45% of normal per-hour compute cost; however, when preemption causes retries onto baseline GPUs we credit at 100% of the affected token-cost differential (simple approach for proposals).
- Proposed burst-credit schedule: if >1% of requests in a given billing window are impacted by preemption events, pro-rate credits for the impacted requests for that day; if >5% at month-end, offer a 10% monthly invoice credit cap tied to incident reviews.
- Need explicit market language in the contract around "warm pool" charges vs burst charges — warm pool is billed as reserved capacity (monthly) even if idle; spot burst billed as usage.

I'll draft the pricing table and attach to the proposal PDF. Quick ask: Grace, can you confirm whether Lumina needs blackout dates for preemption during Nov 21–28? If so we should lock additional non-preemptible shoulder capacity.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Next steps:
- Review the attached playbook/pdf and comment inline by EOD Friday (24 Sep).
- Schedule a calibration call (30 min) next week to align warm-pool sizing and blackout dates — proposed times: Wed 22 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 23 15:00–15:30 PT.

If Lumina confirms no blackout dates for Nov 21–28 we'll keep the current plan; if you need blackout protection we'll surface the incremental reserved capacity and cost.

Attachments: redwood_lumina_capacity_playbook_v1.pdf

Grace O'Connor
